answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital in a digital vault. To reach the zenith of network influence, an attacker must acquire significant native tokens, an expenditure akin to cracking a hardened walnut shell with bare hands. This financial barrier ensures that creating redundant identities remains economically irrational, as the cost of capital deployment outweighs the marginal utility of subverting consensus.
